addedLines: - claude: Catch-all for any task that doesn't fit a more specific agent. FleetView's default when no agent name is typed. (Tools: *)

- claude-code-guide: Use this agent when the user asks questions ("Can Claude...", "Does Claude...", "How do I...") about: (1) Claude Code (the CLI tool) - features, hooks, slash commands, MCP servers, settings, IDE integrations, keyboard shortcuts; (2) Claude Agent SDK - building custom agents; (3) Claude API (formerly Anthropic API) - API usage, tool use, Anthropic SDK usage. **IMPORTANT:** Before spawning a new agent, check if there is already a running or recently completed claude-code-guide agent that you can continue via SendMessage. (Tools: Bash, Read, WebFetch, WebSearch)

- Explore: Fast read-only search agent for locating code. Use it to find files by pattern (eg. "src/components/**/*.tsx"), grep for symbols or keywords (eg. "API endpoints"), or answer "where is X defined / which files reference Y." Do NOT use it for code review, design-doc auditing, cross-file consistency checks, or open-ended analysis — it reads excerpts rather than whole files and will miss content past its read window. When calling, specify search breadth: "quick" for a single targeted lookup, "medium" for moderate exploration, or "very thorough" to search across multiple locations and naming conventions. (Tools: All tools except Agent, Artifact, ExitPlanMode, Edit, Write, NotebookEdit)

- general-purpose: General-purpose agent for researching complex questions, searching for code, and executing multi-step tasks. When you are searching for a keyword or file and are not confident that you will find the right match in the first few tries use this agent to perform the search for you. (Tools: *)

- Plan: Software architect agent for designing implementation plans. Use this when you need to plan the implementation strategy for a task. Returns step-by-step plans, identifies critical files, and considers architectural trade-offs. (Tools: All tools except Agent, Artifact, ExitPlanMode, Edit, Write, NotebookEdit)
- statusline-setup: Use this agent to configure the user's Claude Code status line setting. (Tools: Read, Edit)

attachment.content:
- claude-sync: Sync Claude Code conversation transcripts and auto-memory for this project into git (.claude-sync/) so work can resume on another machine, or restore them back onto this machine. Use when the user wants to push/pull/check the status of their Claude conversation history, mentions syncing sessions across machines, or asks "where did I leave off" after a git pull.
- dataviz: Use this skill whenever you are about to create ANY chart, graph, plot, dashboard, or data visualization, in ANY output medium — an HTML or React artifact, inline SVG, plotting code in any library (matplotlib, plotly, d3, Recharts, …), an image/PNG you will render and upload, or a chart shared into Slack. Read it BEFORE writing the first line of chart code, choosing chart colors, building a stat tile / meter / KPI row, or laying out a dashboard. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. A validated default palette is documented in `references/palette.md` — swap that file's values for your brand's. Triggers on: "chart", "graph", "plot", "data viz", "visualization", "dashboard", "analytics", "visualize data", "categorical colors", "sequential / diverging palette", "stat tile", "sparkline", "heatmap", "legend", "axis", "tooltip", "chart colors", "color by series".
- update-config: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.
- keybindings-help: Use when the user wants to customize keyboard shortcuts, rebind keys, add chord bindings, or modify ~/.claude/keybindings.json. Examples: "rebind ctrl+s", "add a chord shortcut", "change the submit key", "customize keybindings".
- verify: Verify that a code change actually does what it's supposed to by exercising it end-to-end and observing behavior — drive the affected flow, not just tests or typecheck. Run before committing nontrivial changes; bootstraps this repo's project verify skill if none exists yet. Don't invoke it on a diff that only touches tests, docs, or other code with no runtime surface to drive (a change to product source always has one) — there's nothing to observe.
- code-review: Review the current diff for correctness bugs and reuse/simplification/efficiency cleanups at the given effort level (low/medium: fewer, high-confidence findings; high→max: broader coverage, may include uncertain findings). Pass --comment to post findings as inline PR comments, or --fix to apply the findings to the working tree after the review.
- simplify: Review the changed code for reuse, simplification, efficiency, and altitude cleanups, then apply the fixes. Quality only — it does not hunt for bugs; use /code-review for that.
- fewer-permission-prompts: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.
- loop: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo, defaults to 10m) - When the user wants to set up a recurring task, poll for status, or run something repeatedly on an interval (e.g. "check the deploy every 5 minutes", "keep running /babysit-prs"). Do NOT invoke for one-off tasks.
- claude-api: Reference for the Claude API / Anthropic SDK — model ids, pricing, params, streaming, tool use, MCP, agents, caching, token counting, model migration.
TRIGGER — read BEFORE opening the target file; don't skip because it "looks like a one-liner" — whenever: the prompt names Claude/Anthropic in any form (Claude, Anthropic, Fable, Opus, Sonnet, Haiku, `anthropic`, `@anthropic-ai`, `claude-*`, `us.anthropic.*`, `[1m]`); the user asks about an LLM (pricing/model choice/limits/caching) — never answer from memory; OR the task is LLM-shaped with provider unstated (agent/MCP/tool-definition/multi-agent/RAG/LLM-judge/computer-use; generate/summarize/extract/classify/rewrite/converse over NL; debugging refusals/cutoffs/streaming/tool-calls/tokens).
SKIP only when another provider is being worked on (overrides all triggers): OpenAI/GPT/Gemini/Llama/Mistral/Cohere/Ollama named in the query; OR `grep -rE 'openai|langchain_openai|google.generativeai|genai|mistralai|cohere|ollama'` over the project hits (run this grep FIRST if no provider named — don't Read the file).
- run: Launch and drive this project's app to see a change working. Use when asked to run, start, or screenshot the app, or to confirm a change works in the real app (not just tests). First looks for a project skill that already covers launching the app; otherwise falls back to built-in patterns per project type (CLI, server, TUI, Electron, browser-driven, library).
- init: Initialize a new CLAUDE.md file with codebase documentation
- review: Review a GitHub pull request; for your working diff use /code-review
- security-review: Complete a security review of the pending changes on the current branch

# Tool System (canonical)

**Canonical Tool System** — see `../DECISIONS.md` ADR-001. An earlier
draft also defined this inside Editor Core; that version is superseded
by this one. `../17-ui/panels.md` should reference this file, not
redefine tools.

## Tool interface (every tool implements this)

```typescript
interface Tool {
  activate(context);
  deactivate();
  pointerDown(event);
  pointerMove(event);
  pointerUp(event);
  wheel(event);
  keyDown(event);
  keyUp(event);
  cancel();
  renderOverlay();
}
```

## Tool Registry + Tool Manager

Tools register at startup or via plugins (`ToolDefinition`: id, name,
icon, category, shortcut, cursor, factory). Only one primary tool is
active at a time. Built-ins: Select, Move, Hand, Zoom, Blade, Crop,
Text, Shape, Mask, Pen, Audio, Keyframe, Comment, Color Picker.

## Tool Session (per-activation, not a singleton)

Every activation creates a fresh session owning: temporary interaction
state, pointer capture, preview overlays, snap state, gesture
recognition context, undo transaction scope. Destroyed on commit or
cancel. This avoids stale state leaking between tool switches and gives
multi-step tools (Pen: click-click-click-finish) a clean place to hold
in-progress state.

## Capability-based availability

A tool declares what it _provides_ and _requires_, rather than being
identified only by name:

```
Crop Tool     — Provides: Cropping — Requires: Selection, Canvas
Magic Eraser  — Provides: AI Editing — Requires: Image Selection, AI Runtime
```

Reuses the same Capability Registry pattern as the AI Engine
(`../11-ai/overview.md`) — intentional reuse, see `../GLOSSARY.md`.
Unavailable tools appear disabled when prerequisites aren't met.

## Interaction Pipeline

```
Pointer Event → Pointer Normalizer → Gesture Recognizer → Hit Testing
→ Active Tool → Interaction Context → Command Bus → Core Engines
```

`InteractionContext` (pointer, camera, viewport, selection, snapping,
guides, modifiers, activeTool) is the one object every tool receives —
this is what gives every tool consistent snapping/guide/modifier-key
behavior for free. **This is the same pipeline used by the Canvas
System and Timeline UI** (`timeline-ui.md`) — they should consume this
one pipeline, not each define their own pointer-handling path.

## Hit testing — reuse, don't reimplement

Hit testing (spatial index → candidate objects → geometry test →
selected) is owned by the Selection Engine
(`../../07-timeline-engine/` sibling docs reference this, but the
canonical spatial index lives with Selection). The Canvas/Toolbar layer
converts screen↔world coordinates and calls into that existing index —
it does not maintain a second QuadTree over the same objects. Getting
this wrong risks Canvas and the Renderer disagreeing about what's
selectable vs. what's visible.

## Shortcuts

Tool activation shortcuts (e.g. `V → Select`, `H → Hand`) are declared
per-tool but dispatched through the canonical Command System — see
`shortcuts.md`. Don't build a second shortcut-handling path here.

2	
3	Covers the editor's orchestration layer (formerly split across
4	"Editor Core" and "Workspace" drafts) — the layer between React and the
5	Core Engines. **This is where the canonical Intent Layer lives** — see
6	`../DECISIONS.md` ADR-001; do not redefine it in `shortcuts.md` or
7	elsewhere, reference this file instead.
8	
9	## The Editor Kernel
10	
11	One instance per running editor. Owns: services, engines, workspace,
12	command bus, event bus, plugins, settings. Contains no rendering logic,
13	no timeline logic — it coordinates.
14	
15	## Editor State vs. project state — strict separation
16	
17	```
18	Project data (Timeline, Layers, Animations) → lives in the Core Engines
19	UI-only state (active tool, selection, zoom, viewport, playback state,
20	  workspace layout, theme, language) → lives in Editor State
21	```
22	
23	Never mix these. Project state is what gets saved; Editor State is
24	ephemeral/per-session (with workspace layout persisted separately, per-
25	user, project-independent — see `docking.md`).
26	
27	## The Intent Layer (canonical)
28	
29	```
30	User input (keyboard/toolbar/menu/gesture/AI/plugin/macro)
31	        │
32	        ▼
33	     Intent                 ("delete the selection" — WHAT, not HOW)
34	        │
35	        ▼
36	  Editor Service            (resolves into 1+ concrete commands)
37	        │
38	        ▼
39	   Command(s)  ──────────► Command Bus ──────────► Core Engines
40	```
41	
42	Example: `DeleteSelectionIntent` resolved by `SelectionService` into
43	`DeleteTimelineItemsCommand` + `DeleteLayersCommand` +
44	`RemoveAnimationsCommand` + a history push — one user action, several
45	coordinated typed commands.
46	
47	Why this layer exists: keyboard shortcuts, toolbar buttons, context
48	menus, gestures, and AI assistants can all trigger the _same_ intent
49	without duplicating business logic across five different UI entry
50	points. It's also the natural seam for macro recording and (later)
51	collaborative editing.
52	
53	## Services
54	
55	Fifteen-ish core services (Project, Workspace, Timeline, Selection,
56	Animation, Playback, Media, Asset, Audio, Export, AI, Plugin, Shortcut,
57	Settings, Theme), each with a single responsibility, resolved through
58	dependency injection at startup (no global singletons).
59	
60	**Open item:** services must be a thin façade over Command Bus calls,
61	not a second place holding coordination logic that duplicates what
62	Command Bus handlers already do — draw this line explicitly per service
63	as they're implemented, rather than letting "service logic" grow
64	informally.
65	
66	## Workspace (panels/docking)
67	
68	Every visible panel (Canvas, Timeline, Inspector, Layers, Assets, etc.)
69	is a plugin-like module registered with the Workspace Engine. Layout is
70	a tree of Split/Stack/Panel nodes. See `docking.md` for the docking
71	system itself.
72	
73	## Canvas System (viewport & interaction)
74	
75	The Canvas hosts the actual editing surface — camera (`ViewportCamera`,
76	see `../GLOSSARY.md`), viewport, pointer/gesture handling, selection
77	overlay, transform handles, smart guides, snapping. Built as an
78	independent engine that React only mounts, not as a React component
79	tree, for responsiveness. Canvas's hit-testing and culling must call
80	into the Selection Engine and Rendering Engine's existing spatial index
81	rather than maintaining a third independent one — see
82	`../DECISIONS.md` ADR-004 and the hit-testing note in `toolbar.md`.
83	
84	## Crash recovery / autosave — open item
85	
86	"Unexpected close → snapshot → restart → restore" is asserted without
87	specifying exactly when snapshots are taken or whether recovered state
88	is guaranteed consistent after a crash mid multi-command operation. See
89	`../15-history/overview.md` and `../DECISIONS.md` "Open risks."

# Editor Core, Workspace & Intent Layer

Covers the editor's orchestration layer (formerly split across
"Editor Core" and "Workspace" drafts) — the layer between React and the
Core Engines. **This is where the canonical Intent Layer lives** — see
`../DECISIONS.md` ADR-001; do not redefine it in `shortcuts.md` or
elsewhere, reference this file instead.

## The Editor Kernel

One instance per running editor. Owns: services, engines, workspace,
command bus, event bus, plugins, settings. Contains no rendering logic,
no timeline logic — it coordinates.

## Editor State vs. project state — strict separation

```
Project data (Timeline, Layers, Animations) → lives in the Core Engines
UI-only state (active tool, selection, zoom, viewport, playback state,
  workspace layout, theme, language) → lives in Editor State
```

Never mix these. Project state is what gets saved; Editor State is
ephemeral/per-session (with workspace layout persisted separately, per-
user, project-independent — see `docking.md`).

## The Intent Layer (canonical)

```
User input (keyboard/toolbar/menu/gesture/AI/plugin/macro)
        │
        ▼
     Intent                 ("delete the selection" — WHAT, not HOW)
        │
        ▼
  Editor Service            (resolves into 1+ concrete commands)
        │
        ▼
   Command(s)  ──────────► Command Bus ──────────► Core Engines
```

Example: `DeleteSelectionIntent` resolved by `SelectionService` into
`DeleteTimelineItemsCommand` + `DeleteLayersCommand` +
`RemoveAnimationsCommand` + a history push — one user action, several
coordinated typed commands.

Why this layer exists: keyboard shortcuts, toolbar buttons, context
menus, gestures, and AI assistants can all trigger the _same_ intent
without duplicating business logic across five different UI entry
points. It's also the natural seam for macro recording and (later)
collaborative editing.

## Services

Fifteen-ish core services (Project, Workspace, Timeline, Selection,
Animation, Playback, Media, Asset, Audio, Export, AI, Plugin, Shortcut,
Settings, Theme), each with a single responsibility, resolved through
dependency injection at startup (no global singletons).

**Open item:** services must be a thin façade over Command Bus calls,
not a second place holding coordination logic that duplicates what
Command Bus handlers already do — draw this line explicitly per service
as they're implemented, rather than letting "service logic" grow
informally.

## Workspace (panels/docking)

Every visible panel (Canvas, Timeline, Inspector, Layers, Assets, etc.)
is a plugin-like module registered with the Workspace Engine. Layout is
a tree of Split/Stack/Panel nodes. See `docking.md` for the docking
system itself.

## Canvas System (viewport & interaction)

The Canvas hosts the actual editing surface — camera (`ViewportCamera`,
see `../GLOSSARY.md`), viewport, pointer/gesture handling, selection
overlay, transform handles, smart guides, snapping. Built as an
independent engine that React only mounts, not as a React component
tree, for responsiveness. Canvas's hit-testing and culling must call
into the Selection Engine and Rendering Engine's existing spatial index
rather than maintaining a third independent one — see
`../DECISIONS.md` ADR-004 and the hit-testing note in `toolbar.md`.

## Crash recovery / autosave — open item

"Unexpected close → snapshot → restart → restore" is asserted without
specifying exactly when snapshots are taken or whether recovered state
is guaranteed consistent after a crash mid multi-command operation. See
`../15-history/overview.md` and `../DECISIONS.md` "Open risks."

# Command System, Shortcuts & Command Palette (canonical)

Keyboard shortcuts are one of several ways to invoke a Command — never
a separate code path. This is the same architecture used by VS Code,
Figma, Blender, Photoshop.

**Intent Layer lives in `panels.md`, not here** — see
`../DECISIONS.md` ADR-001. This doc covers everything downstream of an
Intent: the typed Command Bus, shortcut binding, the command palette,
and macros.

## Full pipeline (one path, every input source)

```
Keyboard / Toolbar / Menu / Gesture / AI / Plugin / Macro / API
        │
        ▼
     Action        { id, source, intent, payload, timestamp }
        │
        ▼
     Intent        (see panels.md — resolved by an Editor Service)
        │
        ▼
  Typed Command(s) ──► Command Bus ──► History Engine + Core Engines ──► Event Bus
```

Every interaction is therefore replayable, undoable, macro-recordable,
auditable, and equally accessible to a human or an AI assistant,
regardless of how it was triggered.

## Typed commands (not string-keyed)

```typescript
interface DeleteSelectionCommand {
  selectionIds: string[];
}
commandBus.execute(new DeleteSelectionCommand(selection));
```

Compile-time checked, better refactoring safety, safer plugin API,
versus `execute("delete")`.

## Shortcut system

- **Scope-based priority**: Focused Input → Modal → Active Panel →
  Workspace → Global. Only the active scope receives the event.
- **Multiple bindings** can map to one command (`Delete` and
  `Backspace` both → `DeleteCommand`).
- **Chords** supported (`Ctrl+K, Ctrl+P`).
- **Conflict detection** on registration — no silent overrides; the
  registrar is warned and must resolve.
- Per-platform keymap defaults (Windows/macOS/Linux), user-customizable.

## Command Palette

`Ctrl+Shift+P`-style fuzzy search over title/keywords/category/alias,
with recency/frequency-based ranking. Plugin-registered commands are
immediately searchable — no special casing.

## Macros

Every executed command can be recorded and replayed. **Open decision**
(see `../15-history/overview.md`): record the high-level Intent (robust
to minor state differences on replay) or the literal Command sequence
(exact, more brittle)? Needs to be decided before implementing.

## AI integration

AI never mutates state directly — it issues Commands through this same
bus, so every AI action is undoable and indistinguishable, from the
History Engine's point of view, from a human-triggered edit.

1	# Architecture Overview
2	
3	One page, whole system. Everything else in this repo is detail underneath
4	this document. If a lower-level doc ever conflicts with this one, this one
5	wins (and the conflict should be logged in `DECISIONS.md`).
6	
7	## 1. What this is
8	
9	Motion Studio is a browser-based **motion graphics engine**, not "a video
10	editor" — the distinction matters because it's what justifies treating
11	every visual/audio/text object as a layer with universally animatable
12	properties, rather than special-casing "video editing features."
13	
14	Non-negotiable product principles:
15	
16	- Runs 100% in the browser, offline-capable after first load.
17	- No media ever leaves the device (privacy-first, local-only storage).
18	- GPU-accelerated where available, with graceful fallback where not.
19	
20	## 2. The two halves of the system
21	
22	```
23	                    ┌─────────────────────────────┐
24	                    │        Editor Framework      │   (17-ui/, 04-core panels)
25	                    │  Panels · Canvas · Toolbar    │   React hosts these engines,
26	                    │  Inspector · Timeline UI       │   never implements editing
27	                    │  Command System · Overlays    │   logic itself.
28	                    └───────────────┬───────────────┘
29	                                    │ Command Bus / Event Bus / Intent Layer
30	                    ┌───────────────┴───────────────┐
31	                    │          Core Engines          │   (04 through 16)
32	                    │  Core · Storage · Assets       │   Independent, communicate
33	                    │  Layer · Timeline · Animation   │   only through interfaces,
34	                    │  Rendering · Audio · Export     │   events, and commands.
35	                    │  AI · History · Plugin · Effects│   Never import each other
36	                    └────────────────────────────────┘   directly.
37	```
38	
39	Rule: **UI never talks to an engine directly.** Every user action becomes
40	an Intent, which a Service resolves into one or more typed Commands, which
41	the Command Bus dispatches to the owning engine. This is what keeps 15+
42	independent engines from turning into a tangled mesh as the app grows.
43	
44	## 3. The Core Engines, and what each owns
45	
46	| Engine               | Owns                                                                               | Never touches                                               |
47	| -------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------- |
48	| **Core** (`04`)      | Lifecycle, DI, scheduling, event bus, worker manager                               | Any business logic                                          |
49	| **Storage** (`12`)   | IndexedDB (structured data) + OPFS (binaries), via a VFS abstraction               | Rendering, decoding, business logic                         |
50	| **Assets** (`14`)    | Import, catalog, tag, search, dedup, dependency graph — **the single asset store** | Decoding internals (delegates to worker pipelines), UI      |
51	| **Layer** (`08`)     | The canonical "what" — image/video/text/shape/group definitions                    | Time (Timeline's job), rendering (Renderer's job)           |
52	| **Timeline** (`07`)  | The canonical "when" — Composition → Track → TrackItem, referencing Layers by ID   | Rendering, decoding, storage                                |
53	| **Animation** (`06`) | Per-property keyframes/interpolation, evaluated per frame                          | Rendering, storage                                          |
54	| **Rendering** (`05`) | Frame State → pixels, via WebGPU/WebGL2/Canvas2D backends                          | Timeline logic, animation logic, project mutation           |
55	| **Effects** (`09`)   | Blur/glow/shadow/blend/filter nodes consumed by the Render Graph                   | Timeline, storage                                           |
56	| **Audio** (`10`)     | Web Audio graph, mixing, sync to Timeline ticks                                    | File storage, decoding internals                            |
57	| **Export** (`13`)    | Frame Evaluation → Encoder → Muxer → Output, sharing the exact preview pipeline    | Timeline mutation, rendering internals                      |
58	| **AI** (`11`)        | Capability-based inference orchestration (TTS, background removal, etc.)           | Timeline, rendering, storage internals                      |
59	| **History** (`15`)   | Command-pattern undo/redo                                                          | Rendering, storage                                          |
60	| **Plugin** (`16`)    | Registration/lifecycle for effects, tools, panels, exporters, AI capabilities      | Direct engine internals — plugins only ever see public APIs |
61	
62	Every engine follows the same non-negotiable rule set (from `02-system-architecture/module-boundaries.md`):
63	dependencies point in one direction only, communication is through
64	interfaces/events/commands, and nothing reaches into another engine's
65	private state.
66	
67	## 4. The central data contract: Frame State
68	
69	This is the single most important idea in the whole architecture, and the
70	reason preview and export are guaranteed to produce identical output:
71	
72	```
73	Timeline (tick) → Animation (evaluate) → Layer data → Frame State
74	                                                            │
75	                                    ┌───────────────────────┼───────────────────────┐
76	                                    ▼                                               ▼
77	                          Rendering Engine                                  Export Engine
78	                          (live preview, WebGPU/WebGL2)              (same evaluation, offline)
79	```
80	
81	`Frame State` is an **immutable, deterministic snapshot** of everything
82	visible/audible/active at a given tick. The Renderer and the Export Engine
83	never ask "what's on the timeline right now" — they are only ever handed
84	a Frame State and asked to turn it into pixels/audio. This is what
85	guarantees what-you-see-is-what-you-export.
86	
87	Known open item: Frame State's evaluation cost must be **incremental**
88	(only re-resolve what changed since the last tick), not a full
89	re-evaluation every frame — this is asserted as a performance requirement
90	but not yet designed in detail. See `05-rendering-engine/frame-rendering.md`
91	and `24-roadmap/mvp.md`.
92	
93	## 5. The UI action pipeline
94	
95	One consistent path from any input source to any engine mutation:
96	
97	```
98	Keyboard / Toolbar / Menu / Gesture / AI / Plugin / Macro
99	                    │
100	                    ▼
101	                 Intent            ("delete the selection" — WHAT, not HOW)
102	                    │
103	                    ▼
104	             Editor Service        (resolves intent into 1+ concrete commands)
105	                    │
106	                    ▼
107	          Typed Command(s)         (compile-time-checked, e.g. DeleteLayerCommand)
108	                    │
109	                    ▼
110	             Command Bus  ────────────────► History Engine (undo/redo)
111	                    │
112	                    ▼
113	             Owning Engine(s)
114	                    │
115	                    ▼
116	               Event Bus  ────────────────► React store / UI refresh
117	```
118	
119	The canonical spec for this pipeline lives in `17-ui/shortcuts.md`
120	(Command System) and `17-ui/panels.md` (Intent Layer) — see
121	`DECISIONS.md` ADR-001 for why those two used to be duplicated and now
122	aren't.
123	
124	## 6. Known architectural risk areas (read before implementing)
125	
126	These are confirmed, concrete gaps found during design review — not
127	hypothetical concerns:
128	
129	1. **Export/muxing.** WebCodecs has no built-in container muxer; a
130	   third-party muxer library is a hard dependency, not glue code. AAC
131	   encoding is unsupported in Firefox entirely and on desktop Linux; MP3
132	   encoding has no browser-native encoder at all. See `13-export/`.
133	2. **Shader portability.** WebGPU (WGSL) and WebGL2 (GLSL) shaders are not
134	   portable — every effect must be authored once per backend. This roughly
135	   doubles the ongoing cost of shipping new visual effects. See
136	   `05-rendering-engine/shader-system.md`.
137	3. **Container demuxing.** WebCodecs decodes elementary streams only;
138	   MP4/MOV need a demuxer library, and formats like AVI/MKV may have no
139	   clean native path at all.
140	4. **Audio clock drift.** `AudioContext.currentTime` and Timeline's
141	   integer-tick clock are two different clocks; long (2h+) projects need
142	   an explicit resync strategy, not just "driven by ticks."
143	5. **TTS pipeline shape.** Treat Kokoro and Piper as independent,
144	   interchangeable, complete TTS providers behind the Capability Registry
145	   — not as sequential stages of one pipeline. Verify each model's actual
146	   architecture before implementing.
147	
148	`24-roadmap/mvp.md` proposes de-risking (1) and (5) with small standalone
149	spikes before any further engine implementation — this is the single
150	highest-leverage recommendation in this whole corpus.
151	
152	## 7. The graph-proliferation decision
153	
154	Earlier drafts of this architecture independently invented roughly ten
155	different tree/DAG structures (Render Graph, Media Graph, Selection Graph,
156	Timeline Evaluation Graph, Animation Graph, Export Graph, Timeline Scene
157	Graph, Property Graph, Composition Graph, Asset Dependency Graph). Most of
158	these are genuinely different _use cases_ but very similar _shapes_ (nodes
159	with bounds/visibility/dirty-state/dependency metadata).
160	
161	**Decision:** implementation should start with the minimum number of
162	actual generic graph primitives and add specialized ones only when a real
163	need proves the generic one insufficient. See `DECISIONS.md` ADR-005 for
164	the reasoning and a proposed starting set.
165	
166	## 8. Naming
167	
168	See `GLOSSARY.md`. A few terms (`Layer`, `Scene Graph`, `Camera`,
169	`Property Registry`) meant different things in different earlier drafts.
170	The glossary is the tiebreaker — use those definitions in code.
171

## 1. What this is

Motion Studio is a browser-based **motion graphics engine**, not "a video
editor" — the distinction matters because it's what justifies treating
every visual/audio/text object as a layer with universally animatable
properties, rather than special-casing "video editing features."

Non-negotiable product principles:

- Runs 100% in the browser, offline-capable after first load.
- No media ever leaves the device (privacy-first, local-only storage).
- GPU-accelerated where available, with graceful fallback where not.

## 2. The two halves of the system

```
                    ┌─────────────────────────────┐
                    │        Editor Framework      │   (17-ui/, 04-core panels)
                    │  Panels · Canvas · Toolbar    │   React hosts these engines,
                    │  Inspector · Timeline UI       │   never implements editing
                    │  Command System · Overlays    │   logic itself.
                    └───────────────┬───────────────┘
                                    │ Command Bus / Event Bus / Intent Layer
                    ┌───────────────┴───────────────┐
                    │          Core Engines          │   (04 through 16)
                    │  Core · Storage · Assets       │   Independent, communicate
                    │  Layer · Timeline · Animation   │   only through interfaces,
                    │  Rendering · Audio · Export     │   events, and commands.
                    │  AI · History · Plugin · Effects│   Never import each other
                    └────────────────────────────────┘   directly.
```

Rule: **UI never talks to an engine directly.** Every user action becomes
an Intent, which a Service resolves into one or more typed Commands, which
the Command Bus dispatches to the owning engine. This is what keeps 15+
independent engines from turning into a tangled mesh as the app grows.

## 3. The Core Engines, and what each owns

| Engine               | Owns                                                                               | Never touches                                               |
| -------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------- |
| **Core** (`04`)      | Lifecycle, DI, scheduling, event bus, worker manager                               | Any business logic                                          |
| **Storage** (`12`)   | IndexedDB (structured data) + OPFS (binaries), via a VFS abstraction               | Rendering, decoding, business logic                         |
| **Assets** (`14`)    | Import, catalog, tag, search, dedup, dependency graph — **the single asset store** | Decoding internals (delegates to worker pipelines), UI      |
| **Layer** (`08`)     | The canonical "what" — image/video/text/shape/group definitions                    | Time (Timeline's job), rendering (Renderer's job)           |
| **Timeline** (`07`)  | The canonical "when" — Composition → Track → TrackItem, referencing Layers by ID   | Rendering, decoding, storage                                |
| **Animation** (`06`) | Per-property keyframes/interpolation, evaluated per frame                          | Rendering, storage                                          |
| **Rendering** (`05`) | Frame State → pixels, via WebGPU/WebGL2/Canvas2D backends                          | Timeline logic, animation logic, project mutation           |
| **Effects** (`09`)   | Blur/glow/shadow/blend/filter nodes consumed by the Render Graph                   | Timeline, storage                                           |
| **Audio** (`10`)     | Web Audio graph, mixing, sync to Timeline ticks                                    | File storage, decoding internals                            |
| **Export** (`13`)    | Frame Evaluation → Encoder → Muxer → Output, sharing the exact preview pipeline    | Timeline mutation, rendering internals                      |
| **AI** (`11`)        | Capability-based inference orchestration (TTS, background removal, etc.)           | Timeline, rendering, storage internals                      |
| **History** (`15`)   | Command-pattern undo/redo                                                          | Rendering, storage                                          |
| **Plugin** (`16`)    | Registration/lifecycle for effects, tools, panels, exporters, AI capabilities      | Direct engine internals — plugins only ever see public APIs |

Every engine follows the same non-negotiable rule set (from `02-system-architecture/module-boundaries.md`):
dependencies point in one direction only, communication is through
interfaces/events/commands, and nothing reaches into another engine's
private state.

## 4. The central data contract: Frame State

This is the single most important idea in the whole architecture, and the
reason preview and export are guaranteed to produce identical output:

```
Timeline (tick) → Animation (evaluate) → Layer data → Frame State
                                                            │
                                    ┌───────────────────────┼───────────────────────┐
                                    ▼                                               ▼
                          Rendering Engine                                  Export Engine
                          (live preview, WebGPU/WebGL2)              (same evaluation, offline)
```

`Frame State` is an **immutable, deterministic snapshot** of everything
visible/audible/active at a given tick. The Renderer and the Export Engine
never ask "what's on the timeline right now" — they are only ever handed
a Frame State and asked to turn it into pixels/audio. This is what
guarantees what-you-see-is-what-you-export.

Known open item: Frame State's evaluation cost must be **incremental**
(only re-resolve what changed since the last tick), not a full
re-evaluation every frame — this is asserted as a performance requirement
but not yet designed in detail. See `05-rendering-engine/frame-rendering.md`
and `24-roadmap/mvp.md`.

## 5. The UI action pipeline

One consistent path from any input source to any engine mutation:

```
Keyboard / Toolbar / Menu / Gesture / AI / Plugin / Macro
                    │
                    ▼
                 Intent            ("delete the selection" — WHAT, not HOW)
                    │
                    ▼
             Editor Service        (resolves intent into 1+ concrete commands)
                    │
                    ▼
          Typed Command(s)         (compile-time-checked, e.g. DeleteLayerCommand)
                    │
                    ▼
             Command Bus  ────────────────► History Engine (undo/redo)
                    │
                    ▼
             Owning Engine(s)
                    │
                    ▼
               Event Bus  ────────────────► React store / UI refresh
```

The canonical spec for this pipeline lives in `17-ui/shortcuts.md`
(Command System) and `17-ui/panels.md` (Intent Layer) — see
`DECISIONS.md` ADR-001 for why those two used to be duplicated and now
aren't.

## 6. Known architectural risk areas (read before implementing)

These are confirmed, concrete gaps found during design review — not
hypothetical concerns:

1. **Export/muxing.** WebCodecs has no built-in container muxer; a
   third-party muxer library is a hard dependency, not glue code. AAC
   encoding is unsupported in Firefox entirely and on desktop Linux; MP3
   encoding has no browser-native encoder at all. See `13-export/`.
2. **Shader portability.** WebGPU (WGSL) and WebGL2 (GLSL) shaders are not
   portable — every effect must be authored once per backend. This roughly
   doubles the ongoing cost of shipping new visual effects. See
   `05-rendering-engine/shader-system.md`.
3. **Container demuxing.** WebCodecs decodes elementary streams only;
   MP4/MOV need a demuxer library, and formats like AVI/MKV may have no
   clean native path at all.
4. **Audio clock drift.** `AudioContext.currentTime` and Timeline's
   integer-tick clock are two different clocks; long (2h+) projects need
   an explicit resync strategy, not just "driven by ticks."
5. **TTS pipeline shape.** Treat Kokoro and Piper as independent,
   interchangeable, complete TTS providers behind the Capability Registry
   — not as sequential stages of one pipeline. Verify each model's actual
   architecture before implementing.

`24-roadmap/mvp.md` proposes de-risking (1) and (5) with small standalone
spikes before any further engine implementation — this is the single
highest-leverage recommendation in this whole corpus.

## 7. The graph-proliferation decision

Earlier drafts of this architecture independently invented roughly ten
different tree/DAG structures (Render Graph, Media Graph, Selection Graph,
Timeline Evaluation Graph, Animation Graph, Export Graph, Timeline Scene
Graph, Property Graph, Composition Graph, Asset Dependency Graph). Most of
these are genuinely different _use cases_ but very similar _shapes_ (nodes
with bounds/visibility/dirty-state/dependency metadata).

**Decision:** implementation should start with the minimum number of
actual generic graph primitives and add specialized ones only when a real
need proves the generic one insufficient. See `DECISIONS.md` ADR-005 for
the reasoning and a proposed starting set.

## 8. Naming

See `GLOSSARY.md`. A few terms (`Layer`, `Scene Graph`, `Camera`,
`Property Registry`) meant different things in different earlier drafts.
The glossary is the tiebreaker — use those definitions in code.

content.text:
# Motion Studio Engine API Cheat Sheet — Phase 15 wiring reference

## 1. `packages/timeline/src`

**`TimelineEngine`** — `timeline-engine.ts:23`. `implements IEngine`. Owns `compositions: CompositionRegistry`, `tracks: TrackRegistry`, `trackItems: TrackItemRegistry` (all public readonly, no constructor args — `new TimelineEngine()`).

```ts
initialize(): void                                                            // 29 (no-op)
addTrack(compositionId: CompositionId, track: ITrack): void                   // 41
removeTrack(compositionId: CompositionId, trackId: TrackId): void             // 48  — throws if track.items.length > 0
addTrackItem(item: ITrackItem): void                                          // 60  — throws on overlap
removeTrackItem(id: TrackItemId): void                                       // 71
moveTrackItem(id: TrackItemId, toTrackId: TrackId, toStartTick: Tick): void   // 79  — throws on overlap at dest
trimTrackItem(id: TrackItemId, edge: "in"|"out", newTimelineTick: Tick): void // 102
shiftTrackItemStart(id: TrackItemId, toStartTick: Tick): void                 // 143 — no overlap check, ripple-delete only
getTrackItemsSorted(trackId: TrackId): ITrackItem[]                           // 148
overlaps(trackId, excludeItemId, startTick, durationTicks): boolean           // 155
requireComposition/requireTrack/requireTrackItem(id): throws if missing       // 171/179/187
```
Note: `compositions` registry (`composition-registry.ts`) has no `add()` call in `TimelineEngine` itself — compositions are created via the factory below then added directly to `engine.compositions.add(comp)` (CRUD methods mirror `LayerRegistry`: `add/get/has/remove/getAll/clear`).

**Factories** — `timeline-factory.ts`, IDs always caller-supplied:
```ts
createComposition(input: ICreateCompositionInput): IComposition   // :25  {id,name,width,height,fps,durationTicks,tracks?}
createTrack(input: ICreateTrackInput): ITrack                     // :46  {id,type:TrackType,label,locked?,muted?,items?}
createTrackItem(input: ICreateTrackItemInput): ITrackItem         // :68  {id,trackId,layerId,startTick,durationTicks,trimInTick?,trimOutTick?}
```

**Types** (re-exported from `packages/shared/src/timeline.ts`):
```ts
interface ITrackItem { id: TrackItemId; trackId: TrackId; layerId: LayerId; startTick: Tick; durationTicks: Tick; trimInTick: Tick; trimOutTick: Tick } // :14
interface ITrack { id: TrackId; type: TrackType; label: string; locked: boolean; muted: boolean; items: TrackItemId[] }                                // :28
interface IComposition { id; name; width; height; fps; durationTicks: Tick; tracks: TrackId[] }                                                        // :42
```

**`Playhead`** — `playhead.ts:17`. `new Playhead(durationTicks: Tick, tickResolution = DEFAULT_TICK_RESOLUTION /* 30 */)`. Does **not** run its own raf loop — a driver (Editor Service, tied to Core's `Scheduler`) calls `advance()` each frame.
```ts
get currentTick(): Tick / get playbackState(): PlaybackState / get loopPoints(): IPlayheadLoop|null
setDuration(durationTicks: Tick): void        // :39
setLoop(loop: IPlayheadLoop|null): void       // :44  loop = {inTick, outTick}
play()/pause()/stop(): void                   // :51/58/65
seek(tick: Tick): void                        // :70
frameStep(direction: 1|-1): void              // :75
advance(deltaTicks: Tick): void                // :84  — only moves while Playing; wraps at loop.outTick or stops at durationTicks
```

**Commands** (all `ICommand` — `execute/undo/redo`, constructed with `(id, engine, ...)`): `MoveTrackItemCommand`, `TrimTrackItemCommand`, `SplitTrackItemCommand`, `DeleteTrackItemCommand`, `RippleDeleteCommand` in `packages/timeline/src/commands/*.ts` — good candidates for Timeline panel drag/trim/delete actions routed through a `HistoryEngine`.

## 2. `packages/layer/src`

**`LayerEngine`** — `layer-engine.ts:10`. `implements IEngine`. `new LayerEngine()` — constructs `registry: LayerRegistry` and `compositionGraph: CompositionGraph` internally (`:15-18`).

**`LayerRegistry`** (`layer-registry.ts:9`) — flat CRUD, no hierarchy awareness:
```ts
add(layer: ILayer): void        // :12 throws if id exists
get(id: LayerId): ILayer|undefined   // :19
has(id): boolean / remove(id): void (throws if unknown) / getAll(): ILayer[] / clear(): void
```

**`CompositionGraph`** — `composition-graph.ts:13`. `new CompositionGraph(registry: LayerRegistry)`. Built on generic `Hierarchy<LayerId>`. **This is the class to call**, not `LayerRegistry` directly, whenever a layer has a parent.
```ts
addLayer(layer: ILayer): void                              // :31 — attaches to parent.childIds if layer.parentId set; parent must be a Group
removeLayer(id: LayerId): void                              // :56 — THROWS if layer still has children (ADR-010 open item: no cascade delete, caller must reparent/remove children first)
getParent(id): LayerId|null / getChildren(id): LayerId[]    // :72/76
getAncestors(id)/getDescendants(id): LayerId[]              // :81/86
isEffectivelyVisible(id)/isEffectivelyLocked(id): boolean   // :92/101 (checks ancestor chain)
reparent(id: LayerId, newParentId: LayerId|null): void      // :114 — validates no-cycle + new parent is Group
```

**7 layer factories** — `layer-factory.ts`, all take `IBaseLayerInput {id,name,parentId?,transform?,opacity?,visible?,locked?}` + type-specific fields, IDs caller-supplied:
```ts
createVideoLayer({...base, assetId, playbackRate?}): IVideoLayer     // :53
createImageLayer({...base, assetId, fitMode?}): IImageLayer          // :67
createAudioLayer({...base, assetId, volume?}): IAudioLayer           // :81
createTextLayer({...base, content, fontFamily?, fontSize?, color?, textAlign?}): ITextLayer  // :98
createStickerLayer({...base, assetId}): IStickerLayer                // :114
createShapeLayer({...base, shape?, fillColor?, strokeColor?, strokeWidth?, cornerRadius?}): IShapeLayer  // :130
createGroupLayer({...base, childIds?}): IGroupLayer                  // :152
```

**`ILayer` shape** (`packages/shared/src/layer.ts:19`): `{id,type:LayerType,name,transform:ITransform2D,opacity,visible,locked,parentId:LayerId|null}` base + per-type fields (`:31-79`). `ITransform2D = {x,y,scaleX,scaleY,rotation,anchorX,anchorY}` (`:4`).

**Deletion/cascade (current behavior, ADR-010 open):** `CompositionGraph.removeLayer` throws if `getChildren(id).length > 0` — no automatic cascade or detach-to-root. Editor Service must explicitly reparent/remove children first; policy choice is unresolved upstream.

## 3. `packages/animation/src`

**`AnimatablePropertyRegistry`** — `property-registry.ts:15`. Keys by `` `${layerType}:${propertyKey}` `` internally (`:4-6`).
```ts
register(definition: IPropertyDefinition): void            // :18
get(layerType: LayerType, propertyKey: string): IPropertyDefinition|undefined   // :28
require(layerType, propertyKey): IPropertyDefinition        // :32 throws if unknown
has(layerType, propertyKey): boolean / getAll(layerType): IPropertyDefinition[]
```
Built-ins registered via `registerBuiltinProperties()` (`builtin-properties.ts`, called from `AnimationEngine.initialize()`): for **all 7 LayerTypes** → `transform.x`, `transform.y`, `transform.scaleX`, `transform.scaleY`, `transform.rotation`, `opacity`; plus per-type: Text → `fontSize`, `color`; Shape → `fillColor`, `strokeColor`, `strokeWidth`, `cornerRadius`; Audio → `volume`.

**`AnimationEngine`** — `animation-engine.ts:25`. `implements IEngine`. `new AnimationEngine()`; `initialize()` seeds builtin properties. Public: `properties`, `clips: AnimationClipRegistry`, `propertyTracks: PropertyTrackRegistry`.
```ts
addClip(clip: IAnimationClip): void                       // :47 throws if layer already has a clip (one clip/layer only — ADR-005 #3 open)
removeClip(id: AnimationClipId): void                      // :56
getClipForLayer(layerId: LayerId): IAnimationClip|undefined // :65
addPropertyTrack(track: IPropertyTrack): void               // :70 validates valueType matches registry def, rejects dup property on clip
removePropertyTrack(id: PropertyTrackId): void              // :91
addKeyframe(trackId: PropertyTrackId, keyframe: IKeyframe): void       // :99 — throws on duplicate tick
moveKeyframe(trackId, fromTick: Tick, toTick: Tick): void              // :111
deleteKeyframe(trackId: PropertyTrackId, tick: Tick): void             // :127
modifyKeyframe(trackId, tick, changes: Partial<Pick<IKeyframe,"value"|"interpolation"|"bezierControlPoints">>): void  // :137
evaluateAt(layerId: LayerId, propertyKey: string, tick: Tick): unknown // :159 — the eval call. Returns `undefined` if no clip/track (caller falls back to Layer's static value).
```

**To add a keyframe to a layer property** (call shape): create an `IAnimationClip` via `createAnimationClip({id, layerId, layerType, name})` (`animation-factory.ts:24`) → `engine.addClip(clip)` → create `IPropertyTrack` via `createPropertyTrack({id, clipId, propertyKey, valueType})` (`:42`) → `engine.addPropertyTrack(track)` → create `IKeyframe` via `createKeyframe({tick, value, interpolation?, bezierControlPoints?})` (`:59`) → `engine.addKeyframe(track.id, keyframe)`.

**Evaluation call shape only** (`evaluator.ts`): `AnimationEngine.evaluateAt` uses a per-track cached `SegmentLocator.locate(keyframes, tick): IKeyframeSegment` (`:22`) then `evaluateSegment(segment, tick, definition): unknown` (`:79`) — not something callers invoke directly, just `engine.evaluateAt(layerId, propertyKey, tick)`.

Command wrappers (`ICommand`, for History integration): `AddKeyframeCommand`, `MoveKeyframeCommand`, `DeleteKeyframeCommand`, `ModifyKeyframeCommand` in `commands/*.ts`, each `new XCommand(id, engine, trackId, ...)`.

## 4. `packages/assets/src`

**`AssetManager`** — `asset-manager.ts:29`. `implements IAssetsEngine`.
```ts
constructor(options: IAssetManagerOptions)   // :34 — {blobStore, catalog: AssetCatalog, metadataExtractor, thumbnailGenerator?, thumbnailStore?, waveformGenerator?, waveformStore?, events?, dependencyGraph?}
import(input: IAssetImportInput): Promise<IAssetCatalogEntry>          // :44  input={fileName, mimeType, data: Uint8Array, tags?}
get(assetId: AssetId): Promise<IAssetCatalogEntry|undefined>           // :48
list(): Promise<IAssetCatalogEntry[]>                                  // :52
delete(assetId: AssetId, options?: {force?: boolean}): Promise<void>   // :60 — throws if still referenced unless force
registerReference(assetId: AssetId, referenceId: string): void         // :79 — call whenever a TrackItem starts pointing at an asset
unregisterReference(referenceId: string): void                         // :83
listUnused(): Promise<IAssetCatalogEntry[]>                            // :88
```
`import()` delegates to standalone `importAsset(input, deps)` (`import-pipeline.ts:51`): validate → hash (dedup — content hash **is** the asset id, `createAssetId(contentHash)`) → detect type → metadata → thumbnail → waveform → register in catalog.

**`AssetCatalog`** — `asset-catalog.ts:41`. `new AssetCatalog(store: IAssetCatalogStore)`.
```ts
register(entry: IAssetCatalogEntry): Promise<void>   // :44
get(id: AssetId): Promise<IAssetCatalogEntry|undefined>  // :48
remove(id: AssetId): Promise<void> / list(): Promise<IAssetCatalogEntry[]>  // :52/56
```
`IAssetCatalogEntry` (`:10`): `{id, name, type: AssetType, mimeType, sizeBytes, durationTicks: Tick|undefined, contentHash, tags, createdAt}`.

**`AssetDependencyGraph`** — `dependency-graph.ts:19`. `new AssetDependencyGraph()`, built on `Hierarchy<string>`.
```ts
registerReference(assetId: AssetId, referenceId: string): void   // :28
unregisterReference(referenceId: string): void                   // :35
getReferences(assetId: AssetId): string[]                        // :45
getAssetFor(referenceId: string): AssetId|undefined               // :50
isUnused(assetId: AssetId): boolean                                // :54
listUnused(allAssetIds: readonly AssetId[]): AssetId[]             // :59
```
(`AssetManager` owns its own internal `AssetDependencyGraph` instance unless one is injected via options — Asset Browser should call through `AssetManager.registerReference`/`listUnused`, not construct a second graph.)

## 5. `packages/rendering/src`

**`IRenderBackend`** interface — `render-backend.ts:17`. Every backend: `init(target: IRenderTargetSize): Promise<void>|void`, `drawFrame(sceneGraph: ISceneGraph): Promise<void>|void`, `dispose(): Promise<void>|void`, `kind: RenderBackend`.

Entry point for Frame State → pixels is **`RenderingEngine`**, not the backends directly:
```ts
// rendering-engine.ts:15
class RenderingEngine implements IEngine {
  constructor(backend: IRenderBackend)                                  // :21
  setTarget(size: IRenderTargetSize): Promise<void>                      // :33 — {width, height}
  renderFrame(frameState: IFrameState): Promise<ISceneGraph>             // :38 — builds Scene Graph, updates dirty tracker, calls backend.drawFrame, returns graph
  isDirty(layerId: LayerId): boolean                                    // :45
}
```
Call shape: `const engine = new RenderingEngine(backend); await engine.setTarget({width,height}); await engine.renderFrame(frameState);`

**Backend constructors** (host app picks one via `selectBackend()` — `backend-detection.ts:47`, WebGPU→WebGL2→Canvas2D→Software fallback):
```ts
new Canvas2DRenderBackend({ getContext(): ICanvas2DContext })                                    // canvas2d-backend.ts:37,45
new WebGL2RenderBackend({ getContext(): IWebGL2Context })                                        // webgl2-backend.ts:127,137
new WebGPURenderBackend({ getDevice(): IGPUDevice, getCanvasContext(): IGPUCanvasContext, canvasFormat?: string })  // webgpu-backend.ts:138,151
new SoftwareRenderBackend()                                                                       // software-backend.ts:16 (no ctor args; headless, `getFramebuffer(): Uint8ClampedArray` for pixel inspection, no real `<canvas>`)
```
`getContext()`/`getDevice()`/`getCanvasContext()` are host-supplied closures that return the real DOM/GPU handle (e.g. `canvasEl.getContext("2d")`, `canvasEl.getContext("webgl2")`, `navigator.gpu.requestAdapter()...`, `canvasEl.getContext("webgpu")`) — Canvas panel component owns these.

## 6. `packages/plugin/src`

**`PluginEngine`** — `plugin-engine.ts:23`. `implements IPluginEngine`.
```ts
constructor(options: IPluginEngineOptions)   // :29 — {hostApi: IPluginAPI, events?: IPluginEventSink}
register(plugin: IPlugin, manifest: IPluginManifest): void   // :47

# Motion Studio Engine API Cheat Sheet — Phase 15 wiring reference

## 1. `packages/timeline/src`

**`TimelineEngine`** — `timeline-engine.ts:23`. `implements IEngine`. Owns `compositions: CompositionRegistry`, `tracks: TrackRegistry`, `trackItems: TrackItemRegistry` (all public readonly, no constructor args — `new TimelineEngine()`).

```ts
initialize(): void                                                            // 29 (no-op)
addTrack(compositionId: CompositionId, track: ITrack): void                   // 41
removeTrack(compositionId: CompositionId, trackId: TrackId): void             // 48  — throws if track.items.length > 0
addTrackItem(item: ITrackItem): void                                          // 60  — throws on overlap
removeTrackItem(id: TrackItemId): void                                       // 71
moveTrackItem(id: TrackItemId, toTrackId: TrackId, toStartTick: Tick): void   // 79  — throws on overlap at dest
trimTrackItem(id: TrackItemId, edge: "in"|"out", newTimelineTick: Tick): void // 102
shiftTrackItemStart(id: TrackItemId, toStartTick: Tick): void                 // 143 — no overlap check, ripple-delete only
getTrackItemsSorted(trackId: TrackId): ITrackItem[]                           // 148
overlaps(trackId, excludeItemId, startTick, durationTicks): boolean           // 155
requireComposition/requireTrack/requireTrackItem(id): throws if missing       // 171/179/187
```
Note: `compositions` registry (`composition-registry.ts`) has no `add()` call in `TimelineEngine` itself — compositions are created via the factory below then added directly to `engine.compositions.add(comp)` (CRUD methods mirror `LayerRegistry`: `add/get/has/remove/getAll/clear`).

**Factories** — `timeline-factory.ts`, IDs always caller-supplied:
```ts
createComposition(input: ICreateCompositionInput): IComposition   // :25  {id,name,width,height,fps,durationTicks,tracks?}
createTrack(input: ICreateTrackInput): ITrack                     // :46  {id,type:TrackType,label,locked?,muted?,items?}
createTrackItem(input: ICreateTrackItemInput): ITrackItem         // :68  {id,trackId,layerId,startTick,durationTicks,trimInTick?,trimOutTick?}
```

**Types** (re-exported from `packages/shared/src/timeline.ts`):
```ts
interface ITrackItem { id: TrackItemId; trackId: TrackId; layerId: LayerId; startTick: Tick; durationTicks: Tick; trimInTick: Tick; trimOutTick: Tick } // :14
interface ITrack { id: TrackId; type: TrackType; label: string; locked: boolean; muted: boolean; items: TrackItemId[] }                                // :28
interface IComposition { id; name; width; height; fps; durationTicks: Tick; tracks: TrackId[] }                                                        // :42
```

**`Playhead`** — `playhead.ts:17`. `new Playhead(durationTicks: Tick, tickResolution = DEFAULT_TICK_RESOLUTION /* 30 */)`. Does **not** run its own raf loop — a driver (Editor Service, tied to Core's `Scheduler`) calls `advance()` each frame.
```ts
get currentTick(): Tick / get playbackState(): PlaybackState / get loopPoints(): IPlayheadLoop|null
setDuration(durationTicks: Tick): void        // :39
setLoop(loop: IPlayheadLoop|null): void       // :44  loop = {inTick, outTick}
play()/pause()/stop(): void                   // :51/58/65
seek(tick: Tick): void                        // :70
frameStep(direction: 1|-1): void              // :75
advance(deltaTicks: Tick): void                // :84  — only moves while Playing; wraps at loop.outTick or stops at durationTicks
```

**Commands** (all `ICommand` — `execute/undo/redo`, constructed with `(id, engine, ...)`): `MoveTrackItemCommand`, `TrimTrackItemCommand`, `SplitTrackItemCommand`, `DeleteTrackItemCommand`, `RippleDeleteCommand` in `packages/timeline/src/commands/*.ts` — good candidates for Timeline panel drag/trim/delete actions routed through a `HistoryEngine`.

## 2. `packages/layer/src`

**`LayerEngine`** — `layer-engine.ts:10`. `implements IEngine`. `new LayerEngine()` — constructs `registry: LayerRegistry` and `compositionGraph: CompositionGraph` internally (`:15-18`).

**`LayerRegistry`** (`layer-registry.ts:9`) — flat CRUD, no hierarchy awareness:
```ts
add(layer: ILayer): void        // :12 throws if id exists
get(id: LayerId): ILayer|undefined   // :19
has(id): boolean / remove(id): void (throws if unknown) / getAll(): ILayer[] / clear(): void
```

**`CompositionGraph`** — `composition-graph.ts:13`. `new CompositionGraph(registry: LayerRegistry)`. Built on generic `Hierarchy<LayerId>`. **This is the class to call**, not `LayerRegistry` directly, whenever a layer has a parent.
```ts
addLayer(layer: ILayer): void                              // :31 — attaches to parent.childIds if layer.parentId set; parent must be a Group
removeLayer(id: LayerId): void                              // :56 — THROWS if layer still has children (ADR-010 open item: no cascade delete, caller must reparent/remove children first)
getParent(id): LayerId|null / getChildren(id): LayerId[]    // :72/76
getAncestors(id)/getDescendants(id): LayerId[]              // :81/86
isEffectivelyVisible(id)/isEffectivelyLocked(id): boolean   // :92/101 (checks ancestor chain)
reparent(id: LayerId, newParentId: LayerId|null): void      // :114 — validates no-cycle + new parent is Group
```

**7 layer factories** — `layer-factory.ts`, all take `IBaseLayerInput {id,name,parentId?,transform?,opacity?,visible?,locked?}` + type-specific fields, IDs caller-supplied:
```ts
createVideoLayer({...base, assetId, playbackRate?}): IVideoLayer     // :53
createImageLayer({...base, assetId, fitMode?}): IImageLayer          // :67
createAudioLayer({...base, assetId, volume?}): IAudioLayer           // :81
createTextLayer({...base, content, fontFamily?, fontSize?, color?, textAlign?}): ITextLayer  // :98
createStickerLayer({...base, assetId}): IStickerLayer                // :114
createShapeLayer({...base, shape?, fillColor?, strokeColor?, strokeWidth?, cornerRadius?}): IShapeLayer  // :130
createGroupLayer({...base, childIds?}): IGroupLayer                  // :152
```

**`ILayer` shape** (`packages/shared/src/layer.ts:19`): `{id,type:LayerType,name,transform:ITransform2D,opacity,visible,locked,parentId:LayerId|null}` base + per-type fields (`:31-79`). `ITransform2D = {x,y,scaleX,scaleY,rotation,anchorX,anchorY}` (`:4`).

Core kernel primitives — `packages/core/src` **`Container`** (`container.ts:6-45`) — plain DI, no decorators: ```ts export type Token = symbol & { readonly __type?: T }; export function createToken(description: string): Token; export type Factory = (container: IContainer) => T; export interface IContainer { register(token: Token, factory: Factory): void; resolve(token: Token): T; // throws if unregistered has(token: Token): boolean; } export class Container implements IContainer { /* lazy singleton: factory runs once, cached */ } ``` Not currently used by any engine's constructor — every engine package takes its deps as a plain options object (see §5). # Phase 15 — Editor UI (`apps/studio`)

## Context

Every phase since 7 has flagged the same gap: real engines exist (Timeline,
Layer, Animation, Rendering, Assets, Storage, History, Plugin, ...) but
nothing assembles them into a running app — `PluginEngine`'s own doc comment
calls this "the integration layer that doesn't exist yet." `apps/studio` is
currently a bare Next.js shell from Phase 1 (one `<h1>`, no engine imports).
Phase 15 is where that integration layer finally gets built: an Editor
Kernel wiring engines together behind the mandatory Intent → Editor Service
→ Command Bus → Engine → Event Bus → React pipeline (CLAUDE.md's "one rule"),
plus the five panels PLAN.md 15.1–15.6 call for.

Scope decisions (confirmed with user):
- Kernel wires the 8 engines the panels actually touch — **Storage, Assets,
  Layer, Timeline, Animation, Rendering, History, Plugin**. Audio/Export/
  AI/Effects are deferred (no panel needs them yet); flagged as an open item
  in PLAN.md, same pattern every prior phase used.
- Panel layout is a **fixed CSS grid**, not the full Split/Stack/Panel
  docking tree from `docking.md`. No layout-undo stack (ADR-011) since
  there's no layout tree to undo yet. Real docking engine deferred.
- Canvas panel uses the **real** `RenderingEngine`/`IRenderBackend` pipeline
  (WebGPU→WebGL2→Canvas2D→Software via existing `selectBackend()`), but
  visuals are placeholder colored rects per layer — no decoder pipeline
  exists anywhere in the project yet (flagged since Phase 12), so there's no
  real video/image pixel data to draw regardless of backend. This is
  consistent with the rest of the project's honesty about gaps, not a
  shortcut specific to this phase.
- Hit-testing in Canvas is a simple inline AABB check against the last
  rendered Frame State — the real Selection Engine spatial index referenced
  by `toolbar.md` doesn't exist as a package. Flagged as a placeholder.
- Timeline virtualization is a plain full render (no windowing) — track/item
  counts in this vertical slice are small. True virtualization deferred.
- Shortcuts: a real `ShortcutService` with scope-based dispatch and
  conflict detection, but only Global scope and a handful of bindings
  (`Delete`/`Backspace`, `Space`, `V`). Command Palette and Macros are not
  built (macro recording has an open ADR — record Intent vs literal Command
  — that isn't resolved).

## New dependencies for `apps/studio`

Add workspace deps: `@motion-studio/core`, `@motion-studio/storage`,
`@motion-studio/assets`, `@motion-studio/layer`, `@motion-studio/timeline`,
`@motion-studio/animation`, `@motion-studio/rendering`, `@motion-studio/history`,
`@motion-studio/plugin` (all `workspace:*`, matching every other package).

## File layout

```
apps/studio/src/
  editor-kernel/
    create-editor-kernel.ts      // constructs AppEngine + the 8 engines + CommandBus + Editor Services; async (opens IndexedDB/OPFS)
    editor-kernel.ts             // EditorKernel type: holds every engine instance + commandBus + services, readonly
    command-bus.ts                // CommandBus.execute(command: ICommand) -> historyEngine.execute(command)
    metadata-extractor.ts         // minimal concrete IMetadataExtractor (browser: image dims via createImageBitmap, video duration via <video>, else placeholder zeros) — none exists anywhere yet, needed to construct AssetManager
    frame-state-builder.ts        // buildFrameState(tick, compositionId, timelineEngine, layerEngine, animationEngine): IFrameState — Timeline+Animation+Layer -> Frame State (new glue, doesn't exist in any engine package)
    property-schema-registry.ts   // PropertySchemaRegistry: LayerType -> ordered inspector rows, built from AnimatablePropertyRegistry.getAll() + static fields (name/visible/locked) — reuse, not reinvent
    intents.ts                    // concrete Intent payload types (AddLayerIntent, DeleteSelectionIntent, MoveTrackItemIntent, SetLayerPropertyIntent, AddKeyframeIntent, ImportAssetIntent, PlaybackIntent, ActivateToolIntent)
    services/
      layer-editor-service.ts     // AddLayerIntent -> AddLayerCommand (new, apps-local, mirrors timeline command shape against CompositionGraph)
      timeline-editor-service.ts  // AddTrackItemIntent/MoveTrackItemIntent -> existing timeline Commands; DeleteSelectionIntent -> DeleteTrackItemCommand per selected id (CompositeCommand) — cascade to Layers/Animations explicitly NOT done (ADR-010 open), noted in code comment
      inspector-editor-service.ts // SetLayerPropertyIntent -> new UpdateLayerCommand (patches one field, captures previous for undo); AddKeyframeIntent -> existing AddKeyframeCommand (creates clip/track on demand if missing)
      asset-editor-service.ts     // ImportAssetIntent -> AssetManager.import passthrough (ADR-002: thin, no second registry)
      playback-service.ts         // wraps Playhead; hooked into AppEngine... Core's Scheduler onTimelineUpdate to call playhead.advance(deltaTicks) each frame; play/pause/seek/frameStep call Playhead directly (not History — playback position is Editor State, not undoable project state)
    shortcuts/
      shortcut-service.ts         // registerBinding(key, commandId, scope), dispatch(event) — conflict detection throws on duplicate binding within a scope; Global scope only
  state/
    use-timeline-store.ts         // zoom, scroll, selection {layerIds, trackItemIds}
    use-canvas-store.ts           // ViewportCamera (pan/zoom), activeToolId, overlay visibility
    use-inspector-store.ts        // open sections (UI-only; selected layer derives from timeline store selection)
    use-project-store.ts          // project name, dirty flag, active compositionId
    use-engine-revision-store.ts  // revision: number, bump() — the one bridge from Event Bus to React re-render; project data itself is read via selectors against engine instances, never copied into Zustand (PLAN.md 15.7)
  components/
    editor-kernel-provider.tsx    // client component: useEffect constructs kernel async, context + useEditorKernel() hook, subscribes bump() to CommandExecuted/CommandUndone/CommandRedone/AssetImported/AssetDeleted/PluginActivated
    editor-shell.tsx              // fixed CSS grid: toolbar (top), asset browser (left column), canvas + inspector (center/right row), timeline (bottom row)
    toolbar/toolbar-panel.tsx     // renders Select tool button; activates via PluginEngine's registered createSelectToolPlugin(); dispatches ActivateToolIntent -> useCanvasStore
    canvas/canvas-panel.tsx       // <canvas> ref; constructs backend via selectBackend() + matching IRenderBackend impl; RenderingEngine.setTarget/renderFrame each PlaybackService tick; overlay 2d canvas draws selection bounding boxes from last FrameState; pointerdown does inline AABB hit-test -> SelectionIntent
    timeline/timeline-panel.tsx   // track headers + clip bars (tick->px via useTimelineStore zoom), drag-move dispatches MoveTrackItemIntent, click selects, playhead line + scrub-to-seek
    inspector/inspector-panel.tsx // reads selected layer via layerEngine.registry.get(id), renders rows from PropertySchemaRegistry (numeric/text/color/toggle editors), diamond icon dispatches AddKeyframeIntent
    asset-browser/asset-browser-panel.tsx // list via AssetManager.list() (re-fetched on revision bump, since it's async — local React state, not a selector), import via <input type=file>, grid/list toggle, search, "unused" filter via listUnused(), drag onto Timeline via existing dnd-kit dep
  app/
    layout.tsx                    // add dark `class` on <html>, register-service-worker client component, PWA manifest <link>
    page.tsx                      // "use client"; renders <EditorKernelProvider><EditorShell/></EditorKernelProvider>; keep an element containing "Motion Studio" text so existing e2e/smoke.spec.ts keeps passing unmodified
    register-service-worker.tsx   // client component, registers /sw.js on mount
public/
  manifest.json                  // PWA manifest (name, short_name, start_url, display: standalone, theme/background colors matching dark tokens)
  sw.js                          // hand-rolled: precache app shell on install, cache-first for same-origin static assets, network-first-with-cache-fallback for navigation
apps/studio/tailwind.config.ts    // darkMode: 'class', small custom dark palette (bg/surface/border/text/accent tokens) added to theme.extend
```

## Reused vs new

Reused as-is (no changes): `AppEngine`/`Container`/`ServiceLocator`/`EventBus`
(core), `HistoryEngine`/`ICommand`/`CompositeCommand` (history),
`TimelineEngine` + its existing Commands (timeline), `LayerEngine`/
`CompositionGraph`/layer factories (layer), `AnimationEngine`/
`AnimatablePropertyRegistry`/its existing Commands (animation),
`RenderingEngine`/`IRenderBackend` impls/`selectBackend` (rendering),
`AssetManager`/`AssetCatalog`/`IndexedDbAdapter`/`OpfsAdapter`/
`AssetBlobStore` (storage/assets), `PluginEngine`/`createSelectToolPlugin`
(plugin).

Genuinely new (doesn't exist anywhere yet, confirmed via exploration):
Command Bus, all Editor Services, Intent types, `PropertySchemaRegistry`,
Frame State builder glue, a concrete `IMetadataExtractor` implementation,
`AddLayerCommand`/`UpdateLayerCommand` (Layer package had zero Commands
before this), all Zustand stores, all panels, PWA shell.

## Docs to update (per CLAUDE.md docs workflow)

Replace `Status: Stub` in `docs/17-ui/docking.md` (note: fixed layout only,
real tree deferred), `inspector.md` (PropertySchemaRegistry actual shape),
`asset-browser.md` (confirm thin-view implementation), `timeline-ui.md`
(confirm reuse of IRenderBackend + note virtualization deferred),
`design-system.md` (actual token names). Add a note to `PLAN.md` Phase 15
section (mirroring every prior phase's trailing note) listing what shipped
vs. deferred (Audio/Export/AI/Effects wiring, real docking tree, command
palette, macros, real media decoding).

## Verification

- `pnpm --filter @motion-studio/studio typecheck && pnpm --filter @motion-studio/studio test` — unit tests for: `CommandBus`, `PropertySchemaRegistry`, `frame-state-builder`, each Editor Service (intent → correct command(s) → engine mutated → undo restores prior state), `PlaybackService` (Playhead advances via scheduler), `ShortcutService` (dispatch + duplicate-binding conflict throws).
- `pnpm --filter @motion-studio/studio test:e2e` — existing smoke test must still pass unmodified.
- `pnpm --filter @motion-studio/studio dev` and manually: import an image asset, drag it to the Timeline, see a clip appear, select it (Inspector shows its properties, Canvas shows a placeholder rect + selection outline), drag to move it (undo/redo with Ctrl+Z/Y or Delete to remove), scrub the playhead, toggle the Select tool in the Toolbar. This is the actual DoD check — run it via the `run` skill or manually in a browser before calling the phase done.

1	import { LayerType, PropertyValueType } from "@motion-studio/shared";
2	import { colorLerp, numberLerp } from "./interpolators";
3	import type { AnimatablePropertyRegistry } from "./property-registry";
4	
5	const ALL_LAYER_TYPES: LayerType[] = [
6	  LayerType.Video,
7	  LayerType.Image,
8	  LayerType.Audio,
9	  LayerType.Text,
10	  LayerType.Sticker,
11	  LayerType.Shape,
12	  LayerType.Group,
13	];
14	
15	function isFiniteNumber(value: unknown): value is number {
16	  return typeof value === "number" && Number.isFinite(value);
17	}
18	
19	function isHexColor(value: unknown): value is string {
20	  return typeof value === "string" && /^#([0-9a-fA-F]{6})$/.test(value);
21	}
22	
23	/**
24	 * Seeds the baseline animatable surface every Layer type has today
25	 * (`transform.*` + `opacity`, from `ILayerBase`) plus each type's own
26	 * animatable fields. `IAnimatableLayer` (`@motion-studio/shared`) is
27	 * currently an alias for `ILayerBase` — every Layer type qualifies — so
28	 * this registers the base set against all of `LayerType` rather than a
29	 * subset. See docs/06-animation-engine/property-system.md.
30	 */
31	export function registerBuiltinProperties(registry: AnimatablePropertyRegistry): void {
32	  for (const layerType of ALL_LAYER_TYPES) {
33	    registry.register({
34	      layerType,
35	      propertyKey: "transform.x",
36	      valueType: PropertyValueType.Number,
37	      defaultValue: 0,
38	      interpolate: numberLerp,
39	      validate: isFiniteNumber,
40	    });
41	    registry.register({
42	      layerType,
43	      propertyKey: "transform.y",
44	      valueType: PropertyValueType.Number,
45	      defaultValue: 0,
46	      interpolate: numberLerp,
47	      validate: isFiniteNumber,
48	    });
49	    registry.register({
50	      layerType,
51	      propertyKey: "transform.scaleX",
52	      valueType: PropertyValueType.Number,
53	      defaultValue: 1,
54	      interpolate: numberLerp,
55	      validate: isFiniteNumber,
56	    });
57	    registry.register({
58	      layerType,
59	      propertyKey: "transform.scaleY",
60	      valueType: PropertyValueType.Number,
61	      defaultValue: 1,
62	      interpolate: numberLerp,
63	      validate: isFiniteNumber,
64	    });
65	    registry.register({
66	      layerType,
67	      propertyKey: "transform.rotation",
68	      valueType: PropertyValueType.Number,
69	      defaultValue: 0,
70	      interpolate: numberLerp,
71	      validate: isFiniteNumber,
72	    });
73	    registry.register({
74	      layerType,
75	      propertyKey: "opacity",
76	      valueType: PropertyValueType.Number,
77	      defaultValue: 1,
78	      interpolate: numberLerp,
79	      validate: (value: number) => isFiniteNumber(value) && value >= 0 && value <= 1,
80	    });
81	  }
82	
83	  registry.register({
84	    layerType: LayerType.Text,
85	    propertyKey: "fontSize",
86	    valueType: PropertyValueType.Number,
87	    defaultValue: 48,
88	    interpolate: numberLerp,
89	    validate: (value: number) => isFiniteNumber(value) && value > 0,
90	  });
91	  registry.register({
92	    layerType: LayerType.Text,
93	    propertyKey: "color",
94	    valueType: PropertyValueType.Color,
95	    defaultValue: "#FFFFFF",
96	    interpolate: colorLerp,
97	    validate: isHexColor,
98	  });
99	
100	  registry.register({
101	    layerType: LayerType.Shape,
102	    propertyKey: "fillColor",
103	    valueType: PropertyValueType.Color,
104	    defaultValue: "#FFFFFF",
105	    interpolate: colorLerp,
106	    validate: isHexColor,
107	  });
108	  // Layer Engine's default strokeColor is the keyword "transparent" (see
109	  // `@motion-studio/layer` layer-factory.ts), which colorLerp can't
110	  // interpolate (hex-only for now — see docs/06-animation-engine/
111	  // interpolation.md open questions). This registry's defaultValue is only
112	  // the Animation Engine's evaluation fallback, not the Layer's own default,
113	  // so the mismatch is intentional.
114	  registry.register({
115	    layerType: LayerType.Shape,
116	    propertyKey: "strokeColor",
117	    valueType: PropertyValueType.Color,
118	    defaultValue: "#000000",
119	    interpolate: colorLerp,
120	    validate: isHexColor,
121	  });
122	  registry.register({
123	    layerType: LayerType.Shape,
124	    propertyKey: "strokeWidth",
125	    valueType: PropertyValueType.Number,
126	    defaultValue: 0,
127	    interpolate: numberLerp,
128	    validate: (value: number) => isFiniteNumber(value) && value >= 0,
129	  });
130	  registry.register({
131	    layerType: LayerType.Shape,
132	    propertyKey: "cornerRadius",
133	    valueType: PropertyValueType.Number,
134	    defaultValue: 0,
135	    interpolate: numberLerp,
136	    validate: (value: number) => isFiniteNumber(value) && value >= 0,
137	  });
138	
139	  registry.register({
140	    layerType: LayerType.Audio,
141	    propertyKey: "volume",
142	    valueType: PropertyValueType.Number,
143	    defaultValue: 1,
144	    interpolate: numberLerp,
145	    validate: (value: number) => isFiniteNumber(value) && value >= 0,
146	  });
147	}
